decisions.id: W83-a revert and re-tier E2 -> E3
decisions.summary: fillet_polyline drawing each corner as a circular arc of 0054's radius, built and unit-tested, then REVERTED on the cohort. The row is re-tiered E2 -> E3 in audit/overrides.json and its claim stays as found (DRIFTED)
decisions.why: Re-measured this round in a detached worktree at HEAD with audit/reverted/wave83-fillet-radius.patch applied, against the clone (engine = HEAD), with make cohort N=18 SEED=23 (seeds 23-40 and the pinned 901-906). The reference settlement was clean both ways. HEAD: 22/24, refused 33 (WebRefused, a farmhouse off the way network) and 906 (OverlapRefused). Patched: 19/24, refused 23 (WebRefused, needle_loops), 40 (row_rules farm_not_on_its_street), 902 (WebRefused, dangling_ends), 904 (WebRefused, a farmhouse off the way network) and 906 as at HEAD; 33 passes. Every other seed matches. That is m:wave83-fillet-radius-reverted exactly. Under XIII a seed that passed and now fails is a regression whatever the net, so the patch cannot ship as it stands. The Edge Case 'a fix that changes many maps' gives the route: where making the failing map pass takes more than the row's tier, the row takes that work's tier and its claim stays as found. The refusals are in the lane web and the row rules, outside curves.py, so the work is a change across modules, E3 by FR-003. This is the same ruling as W81-a, and waves 69 and 74 before it. The row is re-ordered, not dropped, so 'fix all of it' still reaches it in E3 order, and its own fix text meets the 'waits on a found row'. Wave 81's note ('XIII's FIX remains the expected exit then') binds the RETAKING of reverted rows. This row has not been retaken or reverted before, so the note does not bind this wave. When this row is retaken, seeds 23, 40, 902 and 904 under the true radius are the work.
